newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian holding Iri set to secure 10trln lire loan.
newsitem.headline: Italian holding Iri set to secure 10trln lire loan.

text.p: Italian state holding Iri is set to secure a maximum 10 trillion lire loan from a pool of banks to help the parent company re-organise its debt, an Iri source said on Wednesday.

The source said the financing deal would not result in an increase in the parent's debt level. "Instead it will be used for early reimbursement of debt for an equal amount (to the loan), using the most flexible criteria," he added.
Financial daily MF said on Tuesday the loan would last 18-months, was being offered at market rates and was being organised by investment bank IMI.
Iri Spa's debt fell to about 9.5 trillion lire at the end of 1996 from 22.5 trillion lire previously.
"The (loan) forms part of Iri's plan to bring about a further re-dimensioning of its own debt," the Iri source said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
